title: Harpocrates: Breaking the Silence of CPU Faults through Hardware-in-the-Loop Program Generation
problem: CPUs generate incorrect results due to latent manufacturing defects, variability, marginalities, bugs, and aging, causing Silent Data Corruptions (SDCs) in hyperscaler systems. There is a critical need for automated test generation to detect these faults across different system lifetime stages.
motivation: Recent hyperscaler disclosures of SDCs highlight the severity of known and unknown CPU faults, making detection essential for system reliability and data integrity.
method: Harpocrates employs a hardware-in-the-loop approach that iteratively refines constrained-random functional test programs using a detailed simulation-based microarchitecture engine. The methodology models and grades multiple hardware fault types capable of causing data corruption, adapting to various program generators, ISAs, microarchitectures, and fault types.
key_novelty: Hardware-in-the-loop iterative refinement of test programs using detailed microarchitectural simulation to maximize CPU fault detection, enabling faster generation than hardware-agnostic frameworks.
contributions: Automated methodology for generating short, constrained-random functional test programs maximizing fault detection in CPU structures
Hardware-in-the-loop refinement engine using detailed simulation to iteratively improve test programs
Versatile framework adaptable across multiple program generators, ISAs, microarchitectures, and fault types
Demonstrated superior fault detection and shorter generation times compared to open-source test suites and public frameworks

metrics.speedup: shorter test generation times than hardware-agnostic frameworks
metrics.accuracy: higher fault detection rate across CPU hardware structures

primary_theme: CPU fault detection through automated test generation
